nodes.name: Ni foam pretreatment
nodes.procedure: A piece of commercial Ni foam with a size of 1 cm × 2 cm was carefully pretreated by cleaning successively in diluted hydrochloric acid, acetone, ethanol and deionized water. The Ni foam was then dried at 60 °C.

unit_operations.name: Sequential cleaning

unit_operations.name: Drying
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: The Ni foam was then dried at 60 °C

nodes.source_text: Typically, in order to remove surface oxides, a piece of commercial Ni foam with a size of 1 cm × 2 cm was carefully pretreated by cleaning successively in diluted hydrochloric acid, acetone, ethanol and deionized water. The Ni foam was then dried at 60 °C.

nodes.name: Electrodeposition of Ni microspheres
nodes.procedure: 3D Ni microspheres were electrodeposited on the pretreated Ni foam through a simple electrodeposition process in a two-electrode system using electrolyte consisting of 0.1 M NiCl₂ and 2.0 M NH₄Cl. The pretreated Ni foam was used as the working electrode and a Pt wire was used as the counter electrode. After the electrodeposition at –1.0 A cm⁻² for 600 s, 3D Ni microspheres supported on Ni foam (Ni/NF) were obtained. After drying at 60 °C.

unit_operations.procedure_snippet: electrodeposition at –1.0 A cm⁻² for 600 s

nodes.name: Phosphorization to NiP/NF
nodes.procedure: After drying at 60 °C, the obtained Ni/NF was heated at 400 °C for 2 h under nitrogen (N₂) flow with 1.0 g NaH₂PO₂·H₂O placed near Ni/NF at the upstream side to obtain nickel phosphide supported on Ni foam (NiP/NF).

unit_operations.name: Phosphorization
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: heated at 400 °C for 2 h under nitrogen (N₂) flow with 1.0 g NaH₂PO₂·H₂O

nodes.source_text: After drying at 60 °C, the obtained Ni/NF was heated at 400 °C for 2 h under nitrogen... to obtain nickel phosphide supported on Ni foam (NiP/NF).

nodes.name: Electrochemical oxidation of NiP/NF
nodes.procedure: NiP/NF was electrochemically oxidized by cyclic voltammetry in the potential range from 150 to 350 mV vs RHE at a scan rate of 100 mV s⁻¹ in 1.0 M KOH, 30 cycles were applied.
nodes.source_text: NiP/NF was electrochemically oxidized by cyclic voltammetry... 30 cycles were applied.

nodes.name: Sulfuration to NiPS/NF
nodes.procedure: Then the sample was heated at 300 °C for 3 h under N₂ flow with 0.8 g powdered sulfur placed near the NiP/NF at the upstream side to obtain the final product nickel phosphide/sulfide microspheres supported on Ni foam (NiPS/NF).
nodes.source_text: Then the sample was heated at 300 °C for 3 h under N₂ flow with 0.8 g powdered sulfur... to obtain the final product nickel phosphide/sulfide microspheres supported on Ni foam (NiPS/NF).

nodes.name: Sulfuration of Ni/NF to NiS/NF
nodes.procedure: A similar sulfuration method was carried out on the Ni/NF to obtain sulfides supported on Ni foam (NiS/NF).
nodes.source_text: A similar sulfuration method was carried out on the Ni/NF to obtain sulfides supported on Ni foam (NiS/NF).

nodes.characterization_summary: NiPS/NF retains 3D microsphere architecture with rougher surface featuring small nanosheets after phosphorization/sulfuration.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The 3D architecture of Ni/NF was retained after the phosphorization/sulfuration process, while the smooth surface of stacked microspheres became rougher featuring amounts of small nanosheets, as shown in Fig. 1(c) and Fig. S3.

X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns of NiPS/NF, NiP/NF and NiS/NF (Fig. 1d) show three prominent peaks located at around 2θ = 44°, 52° and 76°, which can be indexed to (111), (200) and (220) crystal planes of metallic Ni.

nodes.characterization_summary: High-resolution TEM of NiPS/NF shows lattice fringes of 0.221 nm (Ni₂P (111)) and 0.200 nm (NiS₂ (220)).
nodes.evidence_snippet: lattice fringes with an interplanar spacing of 0.221 and 0.200 nm were displayed in the observational region, corresponding to the Ni₂P (111) plane and NiS₂ (220) plane, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: STEM image and elemental mappings show homogeneous distribution of Ni, P, and S, confirming formation of abundant Ni₂P/NiS₂ interfaces.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) image and corresponding elemental mappings of Ni, P and S demonstrate the homogeneous distribution of Ni₂P and NiS₂ on the surface of Ni microspheres...

nodes.characterization_summary: NiPS/NF XPS: Ni 2p at 873.9 eV (Ni²⁺ 2p₁/₂), 855.9 eV (Ni²⁺ 2p₃/₂); P 2p at 130.1 eV (shifted +0.4 eV vs NiP/NF); S 2p at 162.5/161.3 eV; atomic P=10.52%, S=5.74%, Ni₂P/NiS₂ ratio ≈1.8.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Ni 2p spectrum (Fig. 2a) of NiPS/NF displays two core-level peaks at 873.9 and 855.9 eV... The atomic content of P and S in NiPS/NF is 10.52% and 5.74%, respectively.

nodes.evidence_snippet: Raman spectroscopy was also applied (Fig. S23), indicating the formation of oxidized Ni species after long-term stability OER test in alkaline seawater (two strong vibrational modes at 475 and 550 cm⁻¹).
